title: Draupadi's Grief and the Miracle of the Robes
body:
Draupadi's Grief and the Miracle of the Robes

सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज ।
अहं त्वां सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः ।।

"Abandon all varieties of dharmas and simply surrender unto me alone. I shall liberate you from all sinful reactions; do not fear. (Gita XVIII-66)"

With all five brothers reduced to slaves, Shakuni tempted Yudhishthira with a final wager: Draupadi, the beautiful empress of Indraprastha. In a state of complete mental bewilderment, Yudhishthira staked Draupadi and lost. Duryodhana immediately commanded his charioteer Prathikami to drag Draupadi to the assembly to clean the palace floors as a servant-maid. Draupadi, receiving this horrific news, showed immense intellectual fortitude, sending back a profound legal question: 'Did the King wager me after he had forfeited his own freedom, or did he wager me while he was still a free man?'
Enraged by her resistance, Duryodhana ordered his brother Duhsasana to drag Draupadi by her long, dishevelled hair into the open assembly. In that horrific hour, as Draupadi stood weeping, her garment stained, the elder statesmen of the Kurus sat in paralyzed silence, bound by rigid, legalistic definitions of duty. Only the young prince Vikarna stood up, declaring the wager illegal on multiple grounds: that Yudhishthira had no sole right to wager Draupadi as she belonged to all five brothers, and that a slave who has lost his own freedom has no legal capacity to wager anything or anyone.
Karna venomously dismissed Vikarna's defense, commanding Duhsasana to strip the Pandavas of their upper garments and Draupadi of her robes. As Duhsasana violently pulled at her single garment, Draupadi realized that all human protection had completely failed. Letting go of her robe, she raised both hands in absolute surrender (Sharanagati), crying out to Lord Krishna as 'Govinda.' In that instant, a cosmic miracle manifested: as Duhsasana pulled the cloth, an infinite stream of multi-colored silk appeared, winding around her body without end. Duhsasana piled mountains of fabric on the floor until he sank down in absolute exhaustion, unable to strip the devotee protected by the Supreme.
